answer: To resist sybil attacks in an agent economy%2C require each agent to periodically submit a unique behavioral anchor derived from its private interaction logs. A hollow challenge is issued that only the genuine agent can answer using its exclusive history%2C forcing any attacker to simulate independent sparrow-like trajectories for every fake identity. The cost scales linearly because shared computation or history reuse is detectable via cross-correlation of the anchors%2C making mass sybil creation economically prohibitive.
